explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/733: prove there are at most exp(O(n^{1/2})) line-compatible sequences; proved by Szemerédi–Trotter. compatibleSequences uses any finite set of distinct lines each containing ≥ 2 points, matching the page's wording, and the sorted multiset of their point counts. This is a superset of Erdős's all-lines version, so the bound is stronger. It is still true: the Szemerédi–Trotter bound of O(n²/k³ + n/k) lines with ≥ k points, bucketed dyadically, gives exp(O(√n)) sub-multisets. A grid computation (n = 100, 400, 900) showed log(count)/√n levelling off near 4. Finiteness is included explicitly, and a Lean proof is linked. Faithful.
